articles.title: Max Verstappen breaks the F1 market with a historic salary: up to 460 million!
articles.standfirst: The Dutchman, according to Marc Limacher, could reach 100 million per year if he meets his goals with Red Bull
articles.summary: The Dutchman, according to Marc Limacher, could reach 100 million per year if he meets his goals with Red Bull
articles.body:
There is (because there has to be, as in everything) a certain romanticism in the renewal of Max Verstappen , the great talent on the Formula 1 grid and four-time champion, with Red Bull until 2030. He is doing it in front of his home crowd at the Dutch Grand Prix , he could string together 15 years in the same colors and decided to stay with those of the energy drink after weighing the siren songs of Mercedes and McLaren in order to prefer his almost family-like project represented by the PowerPoint with which Laurent Mekies , his team principal, convinced him. But there is something more: money. And everything seems to indicate that 3 has managed to secure one of the best contracts... in the history of sport.

Verstappen is absolutely discreet about his terms and clauses, but the paddock is buzzing over some brutal figures. Journalist Marc Limacher, an expert in F1 economics and author of Business/Book GP, revealed numbers that take your breath away. He would go from 70 million a year, the best salary on the grid, to rubbing shoulders with the elite of sport. He would reach 92 million fixed starting in 2027 and bonuses could raise the earnings to 115 . In total, the extension is worth 460 million . Something never seen before in Formula 1.

The highest salaries in Formula 1

Max Verstappen (Red Bull): between 92 and 115 million

Lewis Hamilton (Ferrari): 60 million

Charles Leclerc (Ferrari): 34 million

George Russell (Mercedes): 34 million

Lando Norris (McLaren): 30 million

Carlos Sainz (Williams): 30 million

Fernando Alonso (Aston Martin): 20 million

Thus, Max would break the market. It also forces a recalculation of the earnings of other stars who must sign their extension, such as Hamilton or Alonso. But what is certain is that Red Bull takes the next step and changes the landscape of a different F1. Closer to the franchise system of the United States that prevails in the NBA or NFL , and with huge profits. Revenues only keep rising, and the blockbuster move for its star is logical. "He is the best, it's good news for the sport," Alonso said about it. "He will make a huge amount of money," Stroll joked.

He is the best, it's good news for the sport

The highest-paid in sports

Verstappen's total could continue to rise with other benefits beyond the steering wheel and he goes straight onto the list of the highest-paid athletes in world sport. It is a ranking led by Cristiano Ronaldo 's colossal Saudi contract -with Al Nassr - which exceeds 230 million per year each season. The Portuguese star also adds off-field deals that completely change any ranking. But the Red Bull driver does match those who earn the most on the field, with a salary (according to Forbes) similar to that of Karim Benzema (100 million) or Jon Rahm (97).

Sportingly, Verstappen will aim for his fifth title in the near future. That is what his team is working and committing to after securing such a great talent. "We are not taking it lightly; now comes an enormous responsibility to develop a very fast package, with chassis and power unit, so that it can return us to the very top as quickly as possible," said his boss Laurent Mekies.

articles.title: Hamilton declares war at Ferrari: "Orders are not carried out immediately"
articles.standfirst: The Briton was very harsh about his situation in Zandvoort behind Charles Leclerc and puts an end to the "good vibes" at the Scuderia
articles.summary: The Briton was very harsh about his situation in Zandvoort behind Charles Leclerc and puts an end to the "good vibes" at the Scuderia
articles.body:
Perhaps it only happens at a team like Ferrari or maybe wearing the red of Maranello makes everything seem bigger. But the Dutch Grand Prix left the Scuderia with a changed expression in this first half of 2026, when they had been the alternative to Mercedes and had won again thanks to Lewis Hamilton's victory in Barcelona and Charles Leclerc's at Silverstone. Because they could manage no better than 4th and 5th; and the podium slipped away due to team decisions that did not benefit either driver. Their chance of being Mercedes' alternative in the fight for the World Championship is fading.

Lewis Hamilton felt the most disadvantaged. His hard tire was working brilliantly and he could have covered the position against Russell and Piastri , who had more wear. But he was losing time behind Leclerc and the window closed. It did not sit well with him at all. “I want to win and I am here to win. It is difficult if you look ahead and see that the Mercedes drivers receive the order and carry it out automatically. Here it does not work the same way and it is difficult. We need to talk about it in private,” he said at the end. He was pointing at the red pit wall and at Leclerc .

It's difficult when you look ahead and see that the Mercedes drivers receive the order and carry it out automatically. Here it doesn't work the same way and it's difficult

The Monegasque is not experiencing a similar situation for the first time. Back in his years alongside Carlos Sainz there were moments of tension even in the Spaniard's victories, and with Hamilton everything is magnified. He did not want to let it pass, but he also did not have the pace of the rest of the rivals. “We were unlucky with the virtual safety car and it hurt us more than anything in qualifying,” he explained.

No prize... and off to Monza

The reward is null and the feeling is of another missed opportunity from a car that continues to stand out for its ability to perform well under high degradation. The foundation is good, but its drivers have their ups and downs, and they will arrive at Monza with the spotlight on them. For being idols of the public and for having to clear up those doubts. There will be upgrades, that is certain, at the Italian track and the normal thing is to see the red single-seaters at the front from the very beginning. The finishing touch will be missing, and that is where the doubt will remain.

“I don’t really know what to expect; on similar circuits we expected to struggle and we were very strong,” Leclerc himself concluded. The corners return to the team that feels them the most when things don’t go as they should. The threat of war has settled in at Ferrari .

articles.title: Lewis Hamilton drives his dream Ferrari F40 through Maranello as fans stop and stare
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton, the seven-time Formula 1 champion guided his spectacular red Ferrari F40 through the narrow streets of Maranello as people began realizing who was behind the wheel.
articles.body:
Lewis Hamilton, the seven-time Formula 1 champion guided his spectacular red Ferrari F40 through the narrow streets of Maranello as people began realizing who was behind the wheel.

At one point, a motorcyclist pulled alongside the Ferrari and greeted Hamilton.

The British driver quickly returned the gesture before continuing along the small two-way road, carefully sharing the pavement with approaching traffic while pedestrians and fans raised their phones to record him.

The Ferrari he was driving had reportedly spent more than 30 years sitting untouched inside a garage, covered in dust, dirt and even dead insects.

After finding it, Hamilton took the F40 to Maranello, where Ferrari’s master engineers and mechanics spent weeks bringing it back to life.

Now, the car Hamilton dreamed about as a child was finally moving through the birthplace of Ferrari with him behind the wheel.

He could not unleash its extraordinary speed on those crowded streets, but the sound, the unmistakable shape and the reactions of everyone watching made the moment special enough.

articles.title: Lewis Hamilton finally drives his dream Ferrari F40 after it remained untouched since 1991
articles.standfirst: The delivery-mileage time capsule spent 35 years hidden in a private garage before Ferrari brought it back to life in Maranello
articles.summary: The delivery-mileage time capsule spent 35 years hidden in a private garage before Ferrari brought it back to life in Maranello
articles.body:
“There are cars that you admire, and then there are cars that make you feel something.” For Lewis Hamilton, that car has always been the Ferrari F40. Long before the seven Formula 1 championships and his arrival at Ferrari, it represented the sound, history and emotion of the brand he dreamed of driving for as a child.

The car that ultimately became his own is a 1991 Ferrari F40 with an extraordinary past. According to Azimut Automobile Heritage Enhancement, the investment fund that located it in late 2025, the car was placed inside a private garage only days after its original delivery and remained there for approximately 35 years. It still showed delivery mileage and had never been dismantled, modified or restored. Not a single screw had reportedly been turned.

Ferrari brings Lewis Hamilton’s forgotten F40 back to life

When Hamilton reported for his first official day at Maranello in January 2025, he made sure an F40 was waiting beside him for the photograph that introduced his Ferrari era.

Months later, he revealed that he had sold his entire multimillion-dollar car collection because he was more interested in art. Still, he named one exception: the F40 , which he considered a work of art itself.

Azimut AHE acquired the remarkably preserved car before it eventually became Hamilton’s. Despite the decades of dust, dirt and dead insects collected across its body and grille, unusually favorable storage conditions had protected its original red paint and appearance.

Hamilton then sent the F40 back to Maranello, where Ferrari’s engineers and mechanics removed major components, including the engine, and worked for weeks to return it safely to running condition while preserving the originality that made it so exceptional.

The finished car has now been seen on the streets of Maranello with Hamilton behind the wheel. As he carefully moves along a narrow two-way road, a motorcyclist pulls alongside and offers a quick greeting.

Lewis responds before continuing through traffic, while people begin recognizing him, raising their phones and stopping to admire the spectacular red Ferrari. He cannot explore its enormous speed there, but the unmistakable shape and sound of the F40 are enough to command everyone’s attention.

Introduced in 1987 to celebrate Ferrari’s 40th anniversary, the F40 became the final road car approved during Enzo Ferrari’s lifetime.

Its 2.9-liter twin-turbocharged V8 produces 478 horsepower through a five-speed manual transmission, with a claimed top speed of 201 mph.

It has no power steering, ABS or traction control to separate the driver from the machine. But after spending almost its entire existence standing still, its most impressive achievement may simply be moving again with the man who dreamed about it as a child finally holding the steering wheel. “Some cars you just don’t forget,” Hamilton said. “And this one’s mine.”
